title: First Block Story
subtitle: Turn one familiar block into a clear beginning, middle, and ending.
outcome: A 60- to 120-second micro-documentary that shows a place, follows one small change, and ends with a simple visual takeaway.

shotPrompts.title: Open with the whole block
shotPrompts.direction: Stand still and film a wide shot that shows where the story happens: the street, corner, path, or storefronts in one readable frame.
shotPrompts.hint: This is not just scenery. It tells the viewer, 'Here is our world before anything changes.' Hold long enough for someone to understand the place.

shotPrompts.title: Choose one moving subject
shotPrompts.direction: Pick one person, animal, vehicle, shadow, sign, or object in motion and follow it for a few seconds without zooming.
shotPrompts.hint: A story needs a focus. Keep the subject easy to track so the viewer knows what to care about.

shotPrompts.title: Cut closer to a clue
shotPrompts.direction: Film a close detail that explains texture, mood, or routine: hands working, wheels turning, a door sign, cracked paint, passing feet.
shotPrompts.hint: Details make the middle feel specific. Choose something that answers, 'What is this place really like?'

shotPrompts.title: Record the block's sound
shotPrompts.direction: Hold the phone still and capture clean ambient sound from the block: traffic, birds, voices, footsteps, machines, wind, or silence.
shotPrompts.hint: Sound connects shots and helps the edit feel intentional. Avoid talking unless a real voice belongs to the scene.

shotPrompts.title: Find one small change
shotPrompts.direction: Film something that changes from the opening: a person leaves frame, a light shifts, a door opens, traffic clears, rain starts, or a worker finishes a task.
shotPrompts.hint: This is the turn. The change can be tiny, but it should make the viewer feel time passing.

shotPrompts.title: Show the result
shotPrompts.direction: Film what the change leaves behind: an empty bench, a cleaner counter, a quieter corner, a new shadow, or the subject further away.
shotPrompts.hint: The ending should answer, 'What is different now?' Keep the frame simple.

shotPrompts.title: End on a held image
shotPrompts.direction: Choose one calm final frame and hold it without moving until it feels complete.
shotPrompts.hint: Do not add a new idea here. Let the viewer sit with the meaning of the block after the small change.

guidance.structure: Build a simple three-part film: establish the block, observe a small change, then show what the change leaves behind. Each shot should either orient, develop, turn, or resolve the story.
guidance.capture: Shoot vertically for phone-first export. Hold shots steady, avoid fast pans, and use natural light. Capture at least one clean ambient sound clip to bridge the edit.
guidance.assembly: Keep prompts in order. Trim the opening wide shot to orient quickly, let the small-change shot breathe the longest, and end on the held final image. Use straight cuts unless a cut feels confusing.
guidance.export: Export as a private local draft first, then share only after review. Target 90 seconds and never exceed 120 seconds for this template.
